root_cause.text: `nci_transceive()` in the NFC NCI core took ownership of the caller-provided `skb` but failed to free it on early exit paths (`-EPROTO`, `-EINVAL`, and `-EBUSY`), causing a memory leak when those error conditions were hit.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `kfree_skb(skb);` before each of the three early `return` statements in `net/nfc/nci/core.c`, and the commit message explicitly states that these error paths “return without freeing it” and that kmemleak detected leaked `skb` objects.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the transmit skb on all nci_transceive() error paths to prevent memory leaks.
intent_record.what: The function nci_transceive() was changed to call kfree_skb(skb) before returning early in three error paths: when rf_conn_info is NULL, when target_active_prot is not set, and when NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE is already set. The return codes themselves were not changed.
intent_record.how: This ensures the transmit skb is freed on all failure exits instead of leaking it when the exchange cannot proceed, preventing memory/resource leaks during failed NFC data transmissions.

grouping_result.intent: Free the transmit skb on all nci_transceive() error paths to prevent memory leaks.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes nci_transceive() to free the caller-provided skb on all error paths, preventing the memory leak from early exits like -EPROTO, -EINVAL, and -EBUSY.

candidates.rationale: This early exit returns immediately after detecting missing conn_info, but before freeing the caller-provided skb, which matches the reported leak on -EPROTO.
This early exit occurs when no active target is available and previously failed to release skb ownership, causing the leak on -EINVAL.
This busy-path return exits without freeing the transmit skb, directly corresponding to the leaked-buffer error path described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This early return from nci_transceive() on missing conn_info exits without freeing the caller-provided skb, matching the reported leak on the -EPROTO error path.
This early return occurs when no active target is available and previously left the skb owned by the callee unreleased, causing the memory leak on the -EINVAL path.
This busy-path early return exits without freeing the transmit skb, directly corresponding to the leaked-buffer condition described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function `nci_data_exchange()` already has the early-exit handling added by this commit. It now checks `if (test_and_set_bit(NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE, &ndev->flags)) return -EBUSY;` and it stores the callback/context only after that. Most importantly for the leak issue, it calls `rc = nci_send_data(ndev, ndev->conn_id, skb);` and on error executes `if (rc) clear_bit(NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE, &ndev->flags);`, so the transaction state is cleaned up on failure. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is a missing free of the caller-provided skb on early exits in `nci_transceive()`, but that logic is not present in this snippet; instead this code is about protecting concurrent data exchange transactions and already contains the fix for the shown race/cleanup behavior.
